subject: One-off usage settlement & short-term capacity top-up plan
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <agomez@vitalpay.com>
To: Connor Obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Diego Ramirez <dramirez@vitalpay.com>, VitalPay Finance <billing@vitalpay.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Spike in inference hours (Q3) — reconciliation request

Hi Connor,

Hope you’re well. We just finished our internal run-rate check and discovered a ~65% spike in inference hours for the month of September tied to a one-week experiment the fraud team ran. It looks like that usage fell outside our committed bucket and triggered overage billing.

Can you send a reconciliation that shows:
- baseline committed capacity consumed vs. actual for Sept
- per-day breakdown for the spike window (09/14–09/20)
- proposed one-time settlement and whether we can apply any goodwill credit given we’re in the middle of a renewal discussion (Q4 upsell to +30% capacity)

Diego and finance looped me in; they’ll need an invoice/PO-ready statement if we move forward. We’re hoping to resolve quickly so the renewal terms aren’t impacted.

Thanks,
Alicia Gomez
Head of Platform Integrations
VitalPay

From: Connor Obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <agomez@vitalpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, VitalPay Finance <billing@vitalpay.com>, Diego Ramirez <dramirez@vitalpay.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 12:40:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Spike in inference hours (Q3) — reconciliation request

Hi Alicia — thanks for the heads up and for the details. We dug into the logs and attached a reconciliation workbook that contains:
- sheet 1: committed vs actual daily usage (Aug–Oct)
- sheet 2: hourly breakdown for 09/14–09/20 with peak throughput markers
- sheet 3: proposed settlement (one-time charge) and two alternative amortization options (one-time invoice vs. credit spread over 2 months)

Summary (short):
- Net overage for the spike window = 278,400 inference minutes (~4,640 GPU-hours)
- Standard overage unit rate (per GPU-hour) = $45.00
- One-time settlement (gross) = $208,800 before any credits/discounts

Proposal from Redwood:
1) Apply a 15% contract goodwill discount given the pending renewal and the fact this was a short-run experiment: net one-time = $177,480.
2) Offer a billing amortization option: split the net one-time across the next 2 invoices ($88,740 / invoice) if VitalPay prefers smoother cashflow.
3) If VitalPay proceeds with the planned +30% capacity renewal (term starting 2027-01-01), we’ll apply a $25k credit on the first renewal invoice as an additional concession.

Attached: VitalPay_trueup_Q3_usage_breakdown.xlsx (workbook with calc and assumptions).

Next steps: please confirm which billing option you prefer and whether finance needs us to issue an immediate invoice or include the one-time in the Dec renewal invoice. If you want us to generate an invoice/PO now I’ll loop in Marissa for sign-off.

Best,
Connor Obrien
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
phone: +1 415-555-0192

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Connor Obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Alicia Gomez <agomez@vitalpay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, VitalPay Finance <billing@vitalpay.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 08:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Spike in inference hours (Q3) — reconciliation request

Adding finance context — hi Alicia,

We reviewed Connor’s calc. Two operational notes from our side:
- If VitalPay chooses the one-time invoice, we will issue Invoice_VitalPay_20261117_oneoff.pdf with net = $177,480, Net 30 payment terms.
- If you choose the 2-invoice amortization, the first invoice (issued 2026-11-17) will be $88,740 plus any outstanding monthly usage; second amortized invoice will be issued on the regular cycle in Dec.

Please note: for accounting/audit, we’ll include the detailed workbook as supporting attachment and include a short memo describing the experiment window.

If you confirm PO details, we can push the PDF invoice and a payment link (ACH/wire) today and mark it for 2026-Q4 revenue recognition per your preference.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Revenue Operations Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Diego Ramirez <dramirez@vitalpay.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Connor Obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Alicia Gomez <agomez@vitalpay.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 10:17:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Spike in inference hours (Q3) — reconciliation request

Marissa/Connor — thanks for the quick turnaround. VitalPay prefers the amortization option to avoid a one-off cash hit this quarter. Two requests before we finalize:
1) Please revise the workbook to show the amortized amounts on the Dec invoice (line item) and a short memo language we can attach to our GL.
2) We will provide a PO number (VP-PO-1126) — can you confirm the invoice will reference that PO?

If you can issue the first amortized invoice with PO referenced and supporting workbook attached, we’ll route for payment with Net 30.

Diego Ramirez
Director, Finance Operations
VitalPay

From: Connor Obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Diego Ramirez <dramirez@vitalpay.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Alicia Gomez <agomez@vitalpay.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Nov 2026 15:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Spike in inference hours (Q3) — reconciliation request

Diego / Alicia — thanks, understood. We’ll proceed with the amortization path.

Action items completed:
- Updated workbook attached with amortization lines and suggested memo language.
- Invoice created and attached: Invoice_VitalPay_20261117_oneoff.pdf (first amortized installment $88,740). Invoice references PO VP-PO-1126 and lists Net 30 terms.
- As promised: we’ll include the $25k renewal credit on the first renewal invoice once the +30% capacity commit is finalized.

Attachments: VitalPay_trueup_Q3_usage_breakdown.xlsx; Invoice_VitalPay_20261117_oneoff.pdf

Please confirm receipt and we’ll mark the invoice as sent in our billing system.

Best,
Connor Obrien
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
